title: Formal common-refinement and staircase coherence for compactifications
statement:
Let $\mathscr S$ be a category of schemes and separated finite-type morphisms, containing the compactifications and fibre products mentioned below. A compactification of $f:X\to Y$ is a factorization $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow pY$ with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper; a refinement $c'\to c$ is a proper map of ambient schemes over $Y$ restricting to the identity on $X$. Suppose these categories are nonempty and cofiltered (common refinements exist and parallel arrows can be equalized), and compatible compactification towers and common refining towers exist as in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower, lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Suppose the same compatible staircases can be chosen for three composable morphisms.

Assign to each scheme $X$ a category $\mathcal D_X$. To each proper map $p:X\to Y$ assign $P_p:\mathcal D_X\to\mathcal D_Y$, and to each open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ assign $J_j:\mathcal D_U\to\mathcal D_X$, with unital associative natural composition isomorphisms $P_qP_p\simeq P_{qp}$ and $J_kJ_j\simeq J_{kj}$. For every proper/open square $pk=ir$, specify a natural isomorphism $\gamma_Q:J_iP_r\simeq P_pJ_k$, satisfying identity, horizontal and vertical pasting with those compositors, as in the formulas of [lem-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-pasting]. Put $H_c=P_pJ_j$. For a refinement $v:c'\to c$, define $\rho_v:H_c\to H_{c'}$ by $P_p$ applied to $\gamma$ for the square $vj'=j\operatorname{id}_X$, followed by the proper compositor.

The $\rho_v$ satisfy identities and composition, and $\rho_{v_1}^{-1}\circ\rho_{v_2}:H_{c_2}\to H_{c_1}$ for a common refinement $c'\xrightarrow{v_i}c_i$ is independent of that common refinement and its arrows and satisfies the cocycle law. For a compatible tower for $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, write $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $q:\overline Y\to Z$, $a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $r:V\to Y$, and $j:X\hookrightarrow V$ with $bj=a$. The transformation
$$P_qJ_iP_rJ_j\xrightarrow{P_q\gamma_QJ_j}P_qP_pJ_bJ_j\simeq P_{qp}J_a$$
commutes with common-refinement comparisons between any two such towers. For a three-map staircase the two iterated transformations agree under the $\rho$ comparisons and compositors; identity towers give identity transformations. This is a formal assertion about the supplied $P,J,\gamma$ data; it assumes, and does not prove, the geometric existence or invertibility hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, proof after the four displayed equalities: common refining diagrams and the four-square pasting calculation. Agent-formulated formal P,J,gamma version including three-map staircase coherence, extracted from returned step 3.

proof.text:
We compose transformations right to left. All formulas below are between fixed parenthesizations; juxtaposed functors are connected using the supplied proper/open compositors. Their assumed associativity and unit laws identify the different parenthesizations appearing in each displayed formula. For a refinement $v:c'\to c$, write $\tau_v:J_j\to P_vJ_{j'}$ for its square's $\gamma$ after inserting $P_{\mathrm{id}_X}\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\rho_v$ is $P_p\tau_v$ followed by $P_pP_v\simeq P_{pv}$. All its factors are natural isomorphisms. The identity-square axiom gives $\tau_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$. For $w:c''\to c'$, vertical pasting of the two refinement squares gives
$$\tau_{vw}=(P_v\tau_w)\circ\tau_v.$$
Apply $P_p$ and its associative compositor to obtain
$$\rho_{vw}=\rho_w\circ\rho_v.$$
This uses only the pasting and composition identities assumed in the statement.

source.place: Tags 0F7C and 0F7J, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose and lemma-shriek-composition; refinement-square specialization of the supplied axioms

proof.text: Let $v,v':c'\to c$ be parallel refinement arrows. The cofilteredness hypothesis (also stated for precisely this compactification category in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]) gives $t:e\to c'$ with $vt=v't$. Step 1 gives $\rho_t\rho_v=\rho_{vt}=\rho_{v't}=\rho_t\rho_{v'}$. Cancel the isomorphism $\rho_t$ to obtain $\rho_v=\rho_{v'}$. This argument does not assume that refinement arrows are unique or that their open squares are cartesian.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, common-refinement argument; parallel-arrow equalization made explicit

proof.text:
For $v_i:d\to c_i$ put $T_{12}^{d}=\rho_{v_1}^{-1}\rho_{v_2}:H_{c_2}\to H_{c_1}$. A further $t:e\to d$ changes this expression to
$$(\rho_t\rho_{v_1})^{-1}(\rho_t\rho_{v_2})=T_{12}^{d}.$$
For a second common refinement $v_i':d'\to c_i$, choose $s:e\to d$ and $s':e\to d'$ by [lem-cbc-compactifiable-cofiltered]. Step 2 applied to the parallel arrows $v_i s,v_i's'$ gives $\rho_s\rho_{v_i}=\rho_{s'}\rho_{v_i'}$ for each $i$. Substituting these two equalities into the preceding cancellation shows $T_{12}^{d}=T_{12}^{d'}$. This also handles different arrows out of the same common refinement.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, independence of common refining diagrams

proof.text:
For three compactifications, take a common refinement $e$ of all three by applying the pairwise cofilteredness assumption twice. If its arrows are $a_i:e\to c_i$, step 3 lets every comparison be computed on $e$. Hence
$$T_{12}T_{23}=(\rho_{a_1}^{-1}\rho_{a_2})(\rho_{a_2}^{-1}\rho_{a_3})=\rho_{a_1}^{-1}\rho_{a_3}=T_{13}.$$
The same formula gives $T_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $T_{21}=T_{12}^{-1}$. No existence of a categorical limit or smallness of an indexing category is used.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition; elementary cancellation for the cocycle

proof.text:
Consider a refining tower $T_+\to T_-$, writing its proper maps as $h:\overline X_+\to\overline X_-$, $k:\overline Y_+\to\overline Y_-$ and $t:V_+\to V_-$. The exact statement [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] supplies properness of all three maps and the equations
$$h a_+=a_-,\quad k i_+=i_-,\quad t j_+=j_-,\quad h b_+=b_-t,\quad p_-h=kp_+,\quad r_-t=r_+,\quad q_-k=q_+.$$
Let $A$ be the square $(j_+,j_-;\mathrm{id}_X,t)$, $F$ the square $(b_+,b_-;t,h)$, $D$ the square $(i_+,i_-;\mathrm{id}_Y,k)$, and $E$ the square $(a_+,a_-;\mathrm{id}_X,h)$; in this notation the first pair is the top/bottom open maps and the second is the left/right proper maps. Let $B=Q_-$ and $C=Q_+$ be the tower squares $(b_-,i_-;r_-,p_-)$ and $(b_+,i_+;r_+,p_+)$. Every square has open horizontal and proper vertical maps, so its supplied $\gamma$ applies. In particular, no pullback property is needed for $A,D,E,F$.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, the six squares A,B,C,D,E,F of the refinement diagram

proof.text:
The square $E$ is the horizontal paste of $A,F$, since $b_\pm j_\pm=a_\pm$. Horizontal pasting therefore gives
$$\gamma_E=(\gamma_FJ_{j_+})\circ(J_{b_-}\gamma_A).$$
The vertical pastes of $F$ above $B$ and of $C$ above $D$ have the same boundary: top $b_+$, bottom $i_-$, left $r_+$, right $p_-h=kp_+$. Vertical pasting gives the equality
$$(P_{p_-}\gamma_F)\circ(\gamma_BP_t)=(P_k\gamma_C)\circ(\gamma_DP_{r_+}).$$
These are direct instances of the assumed axioms for the squares just listed, including the proper compositors for the equality of the right boundary maps.

source.place: Tags 0F7C, 0F7D and 0F7J; lemma-shriek-composition, final two pasting equalities

proof.text:
Let $\alpha_\pm:H_{g,\pm}H_{f,\pm}\to H_{gf,\pm}$ denote the displayed tower transformations in the statement. Their ingredients are respectively $\gamma_B,\gamma_C$. The refinement comparisons for $f,g,gf$ use respectively $\gamma_A,\gamma_D,\gamma_E$. Naturality of $\gamma_B$ at the morphism $(\gamma_A)_M:J_{j_-}M\to P_tJ_{j_+}M$, for each $M\in\mathcal D_X$, is exactly
$$(P_{p_-}J_{b_-}\gamma_A)\circ(\gamma_BJ_{j_-})=(\gamma_BP_tJ_{j_+})\circ(J_{i_-}P_{r_-}\gamma_A).$$
Expand $\rho_h\alpha_-$ using the first equality of step 6, use this naturality equation, and then use the second equality of step 6, whiskered by $P_{q_-}$ and $J_{j_+}$. The result is
$$\rho_h\alpha_-=\alpha_+\circ(\rho_k\star\rho_t),$$
where $\star$ is the horizontal composite: first change the $f$ factor by $\rho_t$ and then the $g$ factor by $\rho_k$. The identity $q_-k=q_+$ identifies the outer proper functors. The remaining proper and open compositors agree by their supplied associativity and naturality. Thus this is an equality of natural transformations, proved componentwise, not inferred from objectwise invertibility.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, calculation gamma_E gamma_B = gamma_C gamma_D with the naturality interchange written out

proof.text: Given two arbitrary towers, choose a common refining tower as in [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower]. Apply step 7 to its maps to the two towers, and invert the refinement comparisons on the input and output factors. The resulting equation identifies the two $\alpha$ maps under $T$ on each of the three compactification factors. These $T$ maps are independent of the common tower and its arrows by step 3, and compose by step 4. Thus the equation proves the asserted compatibility with all common-refinement comparisons, rather than only with a fixed refining arrow.

source.place: Tag 0F7J, lemma-shriek-composition, reduction from two towers to a common refining diagram

proof.text:
For $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow hT$, use the three-map staircase whose existence is assumed. Write its ambient proper chain as $\overline X\xrightarrow p\overline Y\xrightarrow q\overline Z\xrightarrow sT$, with opens $a:X\to\overline X$, $e:Y\to\overline Y$, $o:Z\to\overline Z$. Write $W$ for the inverse image of $Z$ in $\overline Y$, with maps $k:W\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $u:W\to Z$, and $i:Y\hookrightarrow W$, so $e=ki$. Write $U\subset V\subset\overline X$ for the inverse images of $Y\subset W\subset\overline Y$, with opens $c:U\to V$, $b:V\to\overline X$, $j:X\to U$ and proper maps $r:U\to Y$, $t:V\to W$. Thus $a=bcj$. The staircase supplies properness of $r,t,u,p,q,s$ and the three squares
$$A=(c,i;r,t),\qquad B=(b,k;t,p),\qquad C=(k,o;u,q).$$
They satisfy $tc=ir$, $pb=kt$, $qk=ou$. Their horizontal paste $A+B$ and vertical paste $B+C$ are exactly the squares used for the two composite morphisms. This is the staircase of Tag 0F7K; no geometric existence result is being deduced from the $P,J,\gamma$ axioms.

source.place: Tag 0F7K, lemma-pseudo-functor, the staircase and its three squares

proof.text:
Work first before the final compositors, from $P_sJ_oP_uJ_iP_rJ_j$ to $P_sP_qP_pJ_bJ_cJ_j$. The two iterated tower maps use $A$ then $B+C$, or $C$ then $A+B$. Pasting gives
$$\gamma_{A+B}=(\gamma_BJ_c)\circ(J_k\gamma_A),\qquad\gamma_{B+C}=(P_q\gamma_B)\circ(\gamma_CP_t).$$
After substituting these formulas, the two maps have the common final factor $P_sP_q\gamma_BJ_cJ_j$. Their preceding factors agree by
$$(\gamma_CP_tJ_c)\circ(J_oP_u\gamma_A)=(P_qJ_k\gamma_A)\circ(\gamma_CJ_iP_r),$$
whiskered by $P_s$ and $J_j$. At $M\in\mathcal D_U$ this is precisely naturality of $\gamma_C:J_oP_u\to P_qJ_k$ at the morphism $(\gamma_A)_M:J_iP_rM\to P_tJ_cM$ in $\mathcal D_W$. Composing with the proper/open compositors to $P_{sqp}J_a$ preserves the equality; their two parenthesizations agree by the assumed associativity. This proves the three-map identity on the chosen staircase by two pasting equations and one naturality square.

source.place: Tags 0F7C, 0F7D and 0F7K, lemma-pseudo-functor, final interchange calculation

proof.text: If either iterated construction uses other compatible towers, compare each binary tower with the one induced by the fixed staircase using step 8. Insert those comparison equations in the two composites; every internal $T^{-1}T$ cancels, and step 4 identifies the outside comparisons. Step 10 then identifies the two maps. Thus the identity holds under the stated comparisons for arbitrary choices. For an identity morphism use its trivial compactification and an identity tower. Its interchange square has either both vertical maps identities or both horizontal maps identities, so the identity-square axiom makes $\gamma$ the identity after the supplied unitors. The resulting tower map is the unitor on the other factor. Step 8 transports this statement to other identity towers. This proves both identity laws.
